company_items.summary: AutoZone reported fiscal Q4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO tailwind to gross margins. Domestic comps came in at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1% estimate, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, described as the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex deeper into the Physical AI and robotics perception space.

MillerKnoll reported fiscal Q1 EPS of 53 cents versus the Street at 36 cents, with the beat holding up even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind — adjusted EPS of 42 cents still topped consensus. Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed to $3.88-4.03 billion from $3.93-4.13 billion, while the EPS range was left unchanged at $1.85-2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on through that date to ensure a smooth transition. Hau previously served as CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a management change with no financial guidance update attached.

THOR Industries missed fiscal Q4 EPS at 78 cents versus the Street at 87 cents, with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% against a consensus of 13.85%, though revenue of $2.311 billion slightly topped the Street's $2.17 billion estimate. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressures weighing on retail, and expects a relatively flat retail sales environment in fiscal 2027 without providing formal guidance until later in the fall. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in the North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The data adds meaningful credibility to Viking's position in the competitive GLP-1 obesity drug landscape. This is a significant positive catalyst for the stock.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a pure earnings and company news edition for Tuesday September 22nd — no broad macro or Fed commentary today, so let's go straight to the names moving this morning.

First up, AutoZone beat fiscal fourth quarter earnings with $56.05 per share against the Street's $54.03, but don't get too excited about the quality of that beat. The upside was largely manufactured by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO adjustment adding another 105 basis points. The real business missed — domestic comps came in at plus 1.6 percent versus the Street expecting plus 3.1 percent, and the operating expense ratio worsened 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did say the back half of the quarter showed improving momentum, and they expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027, but this is a mixed print.

Cognex is making a move into Physical AI, announcing the acquisition of RealSense — the depth-sensing camera and robotic perception technology leader — for roughly 500 million dollars upfront plus another 106 million. RealSense is expected to generate 80 to 90 million dollars in revenue, growing more than 50 percent year-over-year. This is a strategic bet on robotics and physical AI infrastructure, and the market will judge whether Cognex is overpaying.

MillerKnoll delivered a cleaner beat — 53 cents per share versus 36 cents expected, and even stripping out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind you get 42 cents, still well above consensus. Sales did miss at $923 million versus the Street's $943 million, and fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed slightly, though the EPS range held. A reasonable print overall.

THOR Industries missed on earnings — 78 cents versus 87 cents expected — with gross margins falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4 percent. Management was candid about the difficult environment, pointing to stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation pressuring household budgets. They won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. That said, North American towable RV order backlog surged roughly 75 percent year-over-year, which is a genuine bright spot to hold onto.

The headline mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics — shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported positive trial results for its GLP-1 obesity drug, showing 22 percent weight loss. That is a strong data readout and puts Viking firmly on the map as a legitimate competitor in the obesity drug space.

Finally, Pentair named a new permanent CFO — Bob Hau, previously CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox — effective November 1st. Routine management transition, nothing alarming there.

Bottom line for today: Viking is the momentum trade on strong GLP-1 data. AutoZone and THOR are cautionary tales about surface-level beats masking real business softness. Stay focused on quality of earnings, not just the headline numbers.
